name: Pale Nile Blue
lede: Pale Nile Blue is a pale blue-green, the pale tone Robert Ridgway charted beside the parent color Nile Blue in his 1912 color atlas.

sections.title: A pale tone of Nile Blue
sections.body:
Pale Nile Blue puts Ridgway's tone word Pale in front of [[nile-blue]], the paired-tone method his 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* used across the atlas [1]. Nile Blue itself is Ridgway's plate XIX, hue 41 prime, tone d, later filed by the ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 in block 163; Maerz and Paul's 1930 *Dictionary of Color* lists it as first recorded in 1884 [1]. Ridgway files both names under his green hues, closer in that system to green than to blue [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[plunket]], 3.1 units off and bluer than this swatch [1]; [[microcline-green]] sits 3.8 units away, reading greener, and [[lichen-green]] 5.3 units away, greener still [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this color in only 33 of 23,781 paintings, 0.14 percent, as photographed; narrowing to at least five percent coverage inside a painting leaves 24 [2]. That makes it rarer than 59 percent of the named colors in our library [2]. It peaks in the 1700s, present in 0.2 percent of the 3,449 paintings from that century, 1.8 times the archive's overall rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light, in 42 percent of its 24 appearances by lightness rank [2].

The earliest match dates to 1478, in a work by Sandro Botticelli, a floor and not a first since the archive's early centuries are thin; that is 434 years before the name's 1912 record, so the match marks a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a surviving pigment [2].
